source_text: Παράγει γὰρ τὸ σχῆμα τοῦ κόσμου τούτου. Καὶ, Ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ παρελεύσονται. Προαναφώνησις τῶν περὶ συντελείας δογμάτων καὶ περὶ τῆς τοῦ κόσμου μεταποιήσεως, τὰ νῦν ἐν βραχέσι κατὰ τὴν στοιχείωσιν τῆς θεοπνεύστου διδασκαλίας παραδιδόμενα. Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεός. Τὰ ἀπὸ χρόνου ἀρξάμενα πᾶσα ἀνάγκη καὶ ἐν χρόνῳ συντελεσθῆναι. Εἰ ἀρχὴν ἔχει χρονικὴν, μὴ ἀμφιβάλῃς περὶ τοῦ τέλους. Γεωμετρίαι γὰρ καὶ ἀριθμητικαὶ μέθοδοι, καὶ αἱ περὶ τῶν στερεῶν πραγματεῖαι, καὶ ἡ πολυθρύλλητος ἀστρονομία, ἡ πολυάσχολος ματαιότης, πρὸς ποῖον καταστρέφουσι τέλος; Εἴπερ οἱ περὶ ταῦτα ἐσπουδακότες συναΐδιον εἶναι τῷ κτίστῃ τῶν ὅλων Θεῷ καὶ τὸν ὁρώμενον τοῦτον κόσμον διενοήθησαν, πρὸς τὴν αὐτὴν δόξαν ἀγαγόντες τὸν περιγεγραμμένον καὶ σῶμα ἔχοντα ὑλικὸν, τῇ ἀπεριλήπτῳ καὶ ἀοράτῳ φύσει, μηδὲ τοσοῦτον δυνη θέντες ἐννοηθῆναι, ὅτι οὗ τὰ μέρη φθοραῖς καὶ ἀλλοιώσεσιν ὑπόκειται, τούτου καὶ τὸ ὅλον ἀνάγκη ποτὲ τὰ αὐτὰ παθήματα τοῖς οἰκείοις μέρεσιν ὑποστῆναι. Ἀλλὰ τοσοῦτον Ἐματαιώθησαν τοῖς διαλογισμοῖς αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐσκοτίσθη ἡ ἀσύνετος αὐτῶν καρδία, καὶ φάσκοντες εἶναι σοφοὶ, ἐμωράνθησαν, ὥστε οἱ μὲν συνυπάρχειν ἐξ ἀϊδίου τῷ Θεῷ τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀπεφήναντο· οἱ δὲ αὐτὸν εἶναι Θεὸν ἄναρχόν τε καὶ ἀτελεύτητον, καὶ τῆς τῶν κατὰ μέρος οἰκονομίας αἴτιον. 1.4 Ἦπου αὐτοῖς ἡ περιουσία τῆς τοῦ κόσμου σοφίας προσθήκην οἴσει ποτὲ τῆς χαλεπῆς κατακρίσεως, ὅτι οὕτως ὀξὺ περὶ τὰ μάταια βλέποντες, ἑκόντες πρὸς τὴν σύνεσιν τῆς ἀληθείας ἀπετυφλώθησαν. Ἀλλ' οἱ τῶν ἄστρων τὰ διαστήματα καταμετροῦντες, καὶ τοὺς ἀειφανεῖς αὐτῶν καὶ ἀρκτῴους ἀπογραφόμενοι, καὶ ὅσοι περὶ τὸν νότιον πόλον κείμενοι τοῖς μέν εἰσι φανεροὶ, ἡμῖν δὲ ἄγνωστοι· καὶ βόρειον πλάτος, καὶ ζῳδιακὸν κύκλον μυρίοις διαστήμασι διαιροῦντες· καὶ ἐπαναφορὰς ἄστρων, καὶ στηριγμοὺς, καὶ ἀποκλίσεις, καὶ πάντων τὴν ἐπὶ τὰ προηγούμενα κίνησιν δι' ἀκριβείας τηρήσαντες· καὶ διὰ πόσου χρόνου τῶν πλανω μένων ἕκαστος τὴν ἑαυτοῦ περίοδον ἐκπληροῖ· μίαν τῶν πασῶν μηχανὴν οὐκ ἐξεῦρον πρὸς τὸ τὸν Θεὸν ἐννοῆσαι ποιητὴν τοῦ παντὸς, καὶ κριτὴν δίκαιον, τὴν ἀξίαν ἀντίδοσιν τοῖς βεβιωμένοις ἐπάγοντα· οὐδὲ τῷ περὶ τῆς κρίσεως λόγῳ τὴν ἀκόλουθον τῆς συντελείας ἔννοιαν ἐπιγνῶναι, ὅτι ἀνάγκη μεταποιηθῆναι τὸν κόσμον, εἰ μέλλοι καὶ ἡ τῶν ψυχῶν κατάστασις πρὸς ἕτερον εἶδος ζωῆς μεταβάλλειν. Ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ παροῦσα ζωὴ συγγενῆ ἔσχε τοῦ κόσμου τούτου τὴν φύσιν· οὕτω καὶ ἡ μέλλουσα τῶν ψυχῶν ἡμῶν διαγωγὴ οἰκείαν τῇ καταστάσει ὑποδέξεται τὴν λῆξιν. Οἱ δὲ τοσοῦτον ἀπέχουσιν ὡς ἀληθέσι τούτοις προσέχειν, ὥστε καὶ πλατὺν γέλωτα καταχέουσιν ἡμῶν περὶ συντελείας τοῦ κόσμου τούτου καὶ παλιγγενεσίας αἰῶνος ἀπαγγελλόντων. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ ἡ ἀρχὴ κατὰ φύσιν προτέτακται τῶν ἀπ' αὐτῆς, ἀναγκαίως περὶ τῶν ἀπὸ χρόνου τὸ εἶναι ἐχόντων διαλεγόμενος, ταύτην ἁπάντων προέταξε τὴν φωνὴν, εἰπὼν, Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν. 1.5 Ἦν γάρ τι, ὡς ἔοικεν, καὶ πρὸ τοῦ κόσμου τούτου, ὃ τῇ μὲν διανοίᾳ ἡμῶν ἐστὶ θεωρητὸν, ἀνιστόρητον δὲ κατελείφθη, διὰ τὸ τοῖς εἰσαγομένοις ἔτι καὶ νηπίοις κατὰ τὴν γνῶσιν ἀνεπιτήδειον. Ἦν τις πρεσβυτέρα τῆς τοῦ κόσμου γενέσεως κατάστασις ταῖς ὑπερκοσμίοις δυνάμεσι πρέπουσα, ἡ ὑπέρχρονος, ἡ αἰωνία, ἡ ἀΐδιος.
thought_title: The world's beginning implies its end
orientation: Basil is arguing against those who think the visible world is eternal, showing that because it began in time it must also end, and that the philosophers' wisdom only increased their condemnation.
pass_a_gloss: For the form of this world passes away. And, Heaven and earth will pass away. A fore-announcement of the doctrines about the consummation and about the transformation of the world, the things now in brief according to the elementary teaching of the God-inspired instruction being handed down. In the beginning God made. The things that began from time, by every necessity also in time must be completed. If it has a temporal beginning, do not doubt about the end. For geometries and arithmetical methods, and the treatises about solids, and the much-talked-about astronomy, the much-busied vanity, toward what end do they turn? If indeed those who have been zealous about these things thought that this visible world also is co-eternal with the Creator of all things God, bringing to the same glory the circumscribed one and having a material body, to the incomprehensible and invisible nature, not even being able to think this much, that of which the parts are subject to corruptions and alterations, of this also the whole by necessity at some time must undergo the same sufferings as its own parts. But they became vain in their reasonings to such a degree, and their foolish heart was darkened, and claiming to be wise, they became fools, so that some declared that heaven co-exists with God from eternity; others declared that it is God, without beginning and without end, and cause of the particular administration. Surely for them the abundance of the wisdom of the world will at some time bring an addition of the harsh condemnation, because seeing so sharply about vain things, they willingly were blinded toward the understanding of the truth. But those who measure the distances of the stars, and catalogue the ever-visible and northern ones of them, and as many as lie around the southern pole, to some they are visible, but to us unknown; and dividing the northern latitude, and the zodiac circle, by countless intervals; and the risings of stars, and stations, and declinations, and the motion of all toward the leading positions having observed with precision; and in how much time each of the wandering stars completes its own circuit; they did not discover one device out of all of them for thinking of God as maker of the universe, and just judge, bringing the worthy recompense to the things lived; nor by the word about the judgment to recognize the following thought of the consummation, that it is necessary for the world to be transformed, if indeed also the condition of souls is going to change to another form of life. For just as the present life had a nature akin to this world; so also the future way of life of our souls will receive an end proper to the condition. But they are so far from attending to these true things, that they also pour broad laughter upon us who announce the consummation of this world and the regeneration of the age. But since the beginning by nature is set before the things from it, necessarily discoursing about the things that have their being from time, he set this word before all things, saying, In the beginning he made. For there was something, as it seems, also before this world, which is contemplable by our mind, but was left unrecorded, because it was unsuitable for those still being introduced and infants according to knowledge. There was some condition older than the generation of the world, befitting the supercosmic powers, the one above time, the eternal one, the everlasting one.

choices.term: Παράγει γὰρ τὸ σχῆμα τοῦ κόσμου τούτου
choices.english: For the form of this world passes away
choices.why: Renders παράγει as present tense 'passes away' to match the ongoing process Basil cites from Paul, and σχῆμα as 'form' to distinguish the world's outward shape from its substance.
rejected: For the fashion of this world is passing away
For the figure of this world departs

choices.why: The glossary and Basil's eschatological context require 'consummation' for the end of the world, not a neutral 'completion'.
Basil uses μεταποίησις for the world's change at the consummation, distinct from destruction; 'transformation' preserves the sense of remaking.

choices.term: ἡ πολυθρύλλητος ἀστρονομία, ἡ πολυάσχολος ματαιότης
choices.english: the much-talked-about astronomy, the much-busied vanity
choices.why: Keeps the rhetorical pairing of epithets with their nouns, and renders ματαιότης as 'vanity' to echo the biblical language Basil is invoking.
rejected: the famous astronomy, the busy emptiness
the much-celebrated astronomy, the laborious futility

choices.why: Renders παλιγγενεσία as 'regeneration' to preserve the technical eschatological term, and αἰῶνος as 'of the age' rather than 'of the world' to keep the temporal sense.
Renders ὑπερκοσμίοις as 'supercosmic' to mark the powers as above the visible world, and δυνάμεσι as 'powers' for the angelic orders.

bible_refs.note: παράγει γὰρ τὸ σχῆμα τοῦ κόσμου τούτου
ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ παρελεύσονται
ἐματαιώθησαν τοῖς διαλογισμοῖς αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐσκοτίσθη ἡ ἀσύνετος αὐτῶν καρδία, φάσκοντες εἶναι σοφοὶ ἐμωράνθησαν

pass_b_english: “For the form of this world passes away” (1 Corinthians 7:31), and “Heaven and earth will pass away” (Matthew 24:35). These are advance announcements of the teachings about the consummation and about the transformation of the world, delivered now in brief as part of the elementary teaching of the inspired Scripture. “In the beginning God made.” Whatever begins from time must of necessity also be completed in time. If it has a beginning in time, do not doubt about its end. For geometry and arithmetic methods, and the treatises about solid bodies, and the much-talked-about astronomy, the much-busied vanity—to what end do they lead? If those who have devoted themselves to these things have conceived that this visible world is co-eternal with God the Creator of all things, bringing what is circumscribed and has a material body to the same glory as the incomprehensible and invisible nature, not even being able to conceive this much: that what has parts subject to corruption and alteration must of necessity one day undergo the same sufferings as its own parts. But they became vain in their reasonings, and their foolish heart was darkened, and claiming to be wise, they became fools (Romans 1:21-22), so much so that some declared that heaven exists together with God from eternity, while others declared that it is itself God, without beginning and without end, and the cause of the particular ordering of things. Surely their abundance of worldly wisdom will one day bring them an increase of their harsh condemnation, because seeing so sharply into vain things, they were willingly blinded to the understanding of the truth. But those who measure the distances of the stars, and catalogue the ever-visible ones and those near the Bear, and all that lie around the southern pole—visible to some, but unknown to us—and who divide the northern latitude and the zodiacal circle into countless intervals, and who observe with precision the risings of stars, their stations, their declinations, and the forward motion of all of them, and how much time each of the wandering stars takes to complete its own circuit—they have not discovered one single device among all these for conceiving of God as the maker of the universe and a just judge who brings to each the worthy recompense for the life he has lived. Nor have they been able, by the teaching about judgment, to recognize the thought of the consummation that follows from it: that the world must of necessity be transformed, if the condition of souls is also to change to another kind of life. For just as the present life has a nature akin to this world, so also the future existence of our souls will receive an end suited to its condition. But they are so far from attending to these truths that they pour out loud laughter at us when we proclaim the consummation of this world and the regeneration of the age. Since the beginning is by nature set before the things that come from it, when he spoke about the things that have their being from time, he necessarily set this word before all others, saying, “In the beginning God made.” For there was something, it seems, even before this world, which is contemplable by our mind but was left unrecorded, because it was unsuitable for those still being introduced and still infants in knowledge. There was a condition older than the birth of the world, befitting the supercosmic powers, the one above time, the eternal, the everlasting.

problems.quote: they could not even grasp this much
problems.why: Greek says 'not even being able to conceive this much' (aorist participle, concurrent with main verb); English 'could not even grasp' changes to finite verb, losing that their inability was concurrent with their vain reasoning.
problems.fix: not even being able to conceive this much

problems.source_quote: ἑκόντες πρὸς τὴν σύνεσιν τῆς ἀληθείας ἀπετυφλώθησαν
problems.why: ἀπετυφλώθησαν is passive 'they were blinded,' not middle 'blinded themselves'; agency is changed from divine/judicial passive to self-inflicted action.
problems.fix: they were willingly blinded to the understanding of the truth
problems.ruling: ἀπετυφλώθησαν is passive 'were blinded'; 'willingly blinded themselves' wrongly makes it reflexive/middle, changing agency.

edits.old: they could not even grasp this much:
edits.new: not even being able to conceive this much:

edits.old: they willingly blinded themselves to the understanding of the truth.
edits.new: they were willingly blinded to the understanding of the truth.

fixed: Changed 'they could not even grasp this much' to 'not even being able to conceive this much' to reflect the Greek aorist participle μηδὲ τοσοῦτον δυνηθέντες ἐννοηθῆναι, which is concurrent with the main verb, not a finite verb.
Changed 'they willingly blinded themselves' to 'they were willingly blinded' because ἀπετυφλώθησαν is passive, not middle.

last_rejected.source_quote: ἑκόντες πρὸς τὴν σύνεσιν τῆς ἀληθείας ἀπετυφλώθησαν
last_rejected.why: Greek is passive 'were blinded,' not middle/reflexive 'blinded themselves'; 'willingly' modifies the passive, not 'willingly blinded' as active
last_rejected.fix: they were willingly blinded, or of their own accord were blinded
last_rejected.ruling: ἑκόντες 'willingly' + passive ἀπετυφλώθησαν 'were blinded' is standard; 'willingly blinded' preserves both elements adequately.

last_rejected.why: πολυάσχολος means 'much-occupied' or 'busy with many things,' not 'much-busied' (passive); the vanity occupies/busies itself with much, not is busied by others
last_rejected.fix: the vanity busy with many things, or the much-occupied vanity
last_rejected.ruling: πολύάσχολος 'much-occupied/busy' rendered as 'much-busied' is within normal range; no meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: bringing what is circumscribed and has a material body to the same glory as the incomprehensible and invisible nature
last_rejected.source_quote: πρὸς τὴν αὐτὴν δόξαν ἀγαγόντες τὸν περιγεγραμμένον καὶ σῶμα ἔχοντα ὑλικὸν, τῇ ἀπεριλήπτῳ καὶ ἀοράτῳ φύσει
last_rejected.why: The participial phrase ἀγαγόντες goes with the subject 'those who have devoted themselves,' but the English dangles: 'bringing... to the same glory' suggests the world is being brought to glory, but the Greek means they are equating/collapsing the world into the same glory as God's nature
last_rejected.fix: bringing the circumscribed and material body into the same glory as the incomprehensible and invisible nature
last_rejected.ruling: ἀγαγόντες with subject understood; 'bringing...to same glory' adequately conveys equating material world with divine nature.

last_rejected.quote: must of necessity one day undergo the same sufferings as its own parts
last_rejected.source_quote: τούτου καὶ τὸ ὅλον ἀνάγκη ποτὲ τὰ αὐτὰ παθήματα τοῖς οἰκείοις μέρεσιν ὑποστῆναι
last_rejected.why: ὑποστῆναι is 'to undergo' or 'to submit to,' but the construction is 'the whole must... undergo the same sufferings as its parts'—the English 'as its own parts' is unclear; it should be 'that its parts undergo' or 'undergone by its parts'
last_rejected.fix: the whole must necessarily one day undergo the same sufferings as are undergone by its own parts
last_rejected.ruling: τὰ αὐτὰ παθήματα τοῖς οἰκείοις μέρεσιν = 'same sufferings as its own parts'; English is clear enough.

last_rejected.quote: while others declared that it is itself God, without beginning and without end, and the cause of the particular ordering of things
last_rejected.source_quote: οἱ δὲ αὐτὸν εἶναι Θεὸν ἄναρχόν τε καὶ ἀτελεύτητον, καὶ τῆς τῶν κατὰ μέρος οἰκονομίας αἴτιον
last_rejected.why: αὐτὸν refers back to 'the heaven' (τὸν οὐρανόν), not 'it' ambiguously; and κατὰ μέρος means 'particular' or 'in parts,' but 'the particular ordering of things' is vague—'the ordering of things in their several parts' or 'the administration of particular things'
last_rejected.fix: others declared that heaven itself is God, without beginning and without end, and the cause of the administration of things in their several parts
last_rejected.ruling: αὐτόν 'it' refers to heaven from context; 'particular ordering' adequately renders τῶν κατὰ μέρος οἰκονομίας.

last_rejected.quote: they have not discovered one single device among all these for conceiving of God
last_rejected.source_quote: μίαν τῶν πασῶν μηχανὴν οὐκ ἐξεῦρον πρὸς τὸ τὸν Θεὸν ἐννοῆσαι ποιητὴν τοῦ παντός
last_rejected.why: μηχανή is 'contrivance,' 'means,' 'expedient,' or 'resource'—'device' is possible but slightly mechanical; more importantly, πρὸς τὸ... ἐννοῆσαι is 'so as to conceive' or 'for the purpose of conceiving,' but the double accusative τὸν Θεὸν... ποιητὴν means 'conceive God as maker,' which the English gets right
last_rejected.fix: they have not discovered one single means among all these for conceiving God as maker of the universe
last_rejected.ruling: μηχανή as 'device' is within normal range; double accusative correctly handled. No real error.

last_rejected.quote: will receive an end suited to its condition
last_rejected.source_quote: οἰκείαν τῇ καταστάσει ὑποδέξεται τὴν λῆξιν
last_rejected.why: λῆξις means 'allotment,' 'portion,' 'heritage,' or 'assignment'—not merely 'end'; it's the appointed lot or destiny. 'End' loses the sense of apportioned destiny
last_rejected.fix: will receive an allotment suited to its condition
last_rejected.ruling: λῆξις can mean 'end/cessation'; context of συντελείας supports 'end' adequately.
